newsitem.title: USA: Mich recount on $79.9 mln school bond referendum.
newsitem.headline: Mich recount on $79.9 mln school bond referendum.

text.p: A $79.7 million school bond referendum narrowly approved by suburban Detroit residents last month survived a recount on Tuesday, the district's community relations director said.

The Plymouth-Canton Community Schools referendum had been approved by 96 votes on March 22. When the Wayne County canvassing board completed their work Tuesday afternoon and certified the election, the margin had dropped to 95, Judy Evola said.

Proceeds from the bonds will go to pay for a new high school and elementary school for the district, which has 15,576 students, Evola said. Consultants have projected that the district will add 746 students over the next five years, she added.
Proceeds from the issue will also be used to upgrade the district's computers for the classroom, replace aging buses and add more buses to the fleet, Evola said.
The longterm building projects will be financed by bonds with maturities of up to 25 years, while by Michigan law, the transportation and computer equipment will be on a seven-year cycle, Evola said.
Thrun, Maatsch & Nordberg has been named bond counsel for the issue, Evola said.

The referendum passed 5,733 votes for to 5,638 votes against in the special election. Another 720 ballots cast were not counted as valid leading to questions about the touch-screen voting machines used in the election.
The machines were to be tested on Tuesday night by the local board of canvassers.
